title: Publish the customer snapshot bucket in the CloudFormation template
description:
**Phase 1 of 5.**

- **Blocked by:** nothing — but sequence it with `chatticus-82dab7`, which is deploying `ChatticusComputers` into the customer account and may surface other template gaps worth batching into one customer-visible change

> **Verified 2026-09-07 against `infra/customer-role.yml`:** the role has **no `s3:` permissions of any kind**. That is why file actions cannot work today, independent of anything else.
>
> It also settles where the bucket should be declared. The role *can* create stacks, but only `ChatticusComputers*` (`cloudformation:CreateStack` scoped to `stack/ChatticusComputers*/*`). CloudFormation creates resources with the **caller's** permissions, so declaring the bucket inside a Chatticus-deployed `ChatticusComputers` stack would still require adding `s3:CreateBucket` to the role. Putting it in the **customer-run template** is the only option that keeps bucket creation off the Anthus role entirely.
- **Unblocks:** file actions in a customer account (`chatticus-3e72dc`)

---

## Decision (2026-09-07)

**Snapshot packs live in the customer's own AWS account, and the bucket is created in advance by the published CloudFormation template.**

Anthus keeps its shared `ChatticusSnapshots` bucket for **Anthus-managed organizations only**. A customer organization's `/workspace` and browser-profile packs never rest in an Anthus-owned bucket.

This is the pitch claim made literal — *their files, their account* — and `chatticus-598be4` calls that the strongest thing on the pitch page.

## Why the template, not the assumed role

Both were on the table. Creating it in advance via IaC wins on four counts:

1. **The customer can read what they are agreeing to.** `chatticus-8a25af` sets the standard: *"the people with authority to grant this will read the policy."* A bucket declared in the template is reviewable before they run it. A bucket conjured later by an assumed role is not.
2. **Chatticus never needs `s3:CreateBucket`.** That is a broad, alarming permission to ask a security team for, and it is exactly the kind of thing that fails the *"why does an agent product need this"* test. Granting write access to one named bucket is a much narrower ask.
3. **No first-run race.** The bucket exists before the first hydrate or publish, so there is no create-on-demand failure path to handle in ComputerWorker.
4. **Clean teardown and lifecycle.** The bucket belongs to the customer's stack. Encryption, versioning and block-public-access are declared, reviewable, and theirs.

## This is a customer-visible template change — do it now

By `chatticus-8a25af`'s own rule, changing the published template means an existing customer has to re-run it. **There are currently no customers, so this change is free today and expensive later.** That is the argument for making it before the beta opens, not after.

The role policy also needs scoping to the new bucket: `chatticus-b88c0a` recorded it as scoped to `ChatticusComputers*` and **not** to any snapshot bucket, which is why file actions cannot work today.

## Why this is permanent, not transitional

`chatticus-fbae4e` D3 was **refuted** on 2026-09-07: `/workspace` stays on host-local disk and the S3 snapshot protocol is the shipping design, not a stopgap awaiting EFS. So this bucket is load-bearing for as long as the product exists. Build it as a first-class part of the template rather than a temporary shim.

## Open sub-questions to settle while writing it

- **Naming.** S3 bucket names are globally unique. `OrganizationId` (the `tenant_id` UUID) is already a template parameter and is the obvious derivation — confirm the resulting name is valid and collision-free.
- **`DeletionPolicy`.** If a customer deletes the stack, should the bucket and their work go with it? `Retain` is the safer default; deleting a customer's files as a side effect of removing an IAM role would be indefensible. Decide explicitly.
- **Region.** The bucket lands in whatever region the stack runs in. The organization computer must run in the same region or pay cross-region transfer on every hydrate and publish. Constrain or document it.
- **Encryption and access.** Declare SSE, versioning, and block-public-access in the template so they are reviewable rather than assumed.
- **Path layout.** `docs/COMPUTER_SNAPSHOTS.md` specifies `s3://…/tenants/{tenant_id}/computers/{computer_id}/`. With one bucket per organization the `tenants/{tenant_id}` prefix may be redundant — decide whether to keep it for symmetry with the Anthus-managed bucket.

## Done when

The published template creates the snapshot bucket, the role is scoped to it, `docs/COMPUTER_SNAPSHOTS.md` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` record which account holds packs for which kind of organization, and the change is recorded as customer-visible.

comments.text:
`chatticus-82dab7` who-creates-what table now points this card for the bucket row. Wiki runbook matches: customer-run published template; assumed role never gets `s3:CreateBucket`; later read/write on one named bucket.

Do not implement this until `chatticus-82dab7` has lab-user `RunTask` evidence. Then this card before `chatticus-3e72dc` file-actions. Wire deps with **full** issue ids.
